samples.summary: Read-only `ensureSlidesRoot` no-op drops the `meta.themeId` ↔ `themes` reconciliation, which `migrateDocument` does NOT perform — `getActiveTheme` then throws for a share-link viewer
samples.evidence: `ensureSlidesRoot` now returns immediately when `options.readOnly` (line 234). The comment and the new test claim `read()` "runs the same backfill in memory through `migrateDocument`", but it does not: `packages/slides/src/model/migrate.ts:80-85` only substitutes `themes = [defaultLight]` / `masters = [DEFAULT_MASTER]` when the raw arrays are absent/empty, and `migrateMeta` (line 32) keeps `m.themeId` verbatim (`?? 'default-light'`). The reconciliation that the skipped write performed — `if (meta.themeId == null || !themes.some(t => t.id === meta.themeId)) meta.themeId = themes[0].id` (yorkie-slides-store.ts:284-295) — has no in-memory counterpart. So for any deck whose `meta.themeId` is not in its (possibly synthesised) `themes` array (e.g. a pre-v0.5 deck with `themeId: 'default-dark'` and no `themes`, or the "partially migrated or customized doc" the original comment at line 279-282 explicitly defends against), a read-only mount yields a `SlidesDocument` where `getActiveTheme` throws (`packages/slides/src/view/canvas/render-context.ts:88-96` — deliberately no fallback), which is reached from `slide-renderer.ts:213` and `editor.ts:4361` on every paint. Before this change the viewer's own mount repaired the document first. The same skip also drops the `slide.notes` / text-element `data.blocks` non-array normalization (lines 296-310), which `migrateSlide` passes through unchanged (`notes: slide?.notes ?? []`, and `migrateElement` only handles `type === 'shape'`). The new test only covers `themeId: 'default-light'`, i.e. the case that happens to match the injected default. Same skip applies on mobile via `mobile-slides-view.tsx:154`.

samples.summary: A read-only sheet now never recalculates cross-sheet formulas, so a viewer can be shown stale cached values indefinitely with no indication
samples.evidence: `recalculateCrossSheetFormulas` returns after a bare repaint when `this._readOnly` (spreadsheet.ts:973-976), and the call site is additionally short-circuited: `runRemoteSync(!readOnly)` (sheet-view.tsx:1308) and `scheduleRemoteSync(readOnly ? false : needsRecalc(ops))` (sheet-view.tsx:1322). Both the initial pass and every remote-change pass are dropped, so a share-link viewer sees whatever cached value the CRDT happens to carry for every `='Other Sheet'!A1`-style formula — including a value another sheet has since invalidated, or none at all for a formula never yet calculated. The recalculation is skipped entirely rather than being performed in memory and simply not persisted, so the displayed number is wrong rather than merely unpersisted. Contained to viewer mounts, but it is a wrong result on a path the feature exists to serve.

samples.summary: Shadow-mode logging calls `.map` on an untyped body field, so a non-array `attributes` turns a computed 403 into a 500
samples.evidence: `const target = (body?.attributes ?? []).map(...)` (line 200). `body` is the raw JSON request body typed only by an interface, so `attributes` may be any JSON value. `?? []` guards only null/undefined: for `attributes: "x"` (or a number/object) `.map` is not a function and the handler throws, returning 500 instead of the 200-with-`allowed:true` that shadow mode promises — and `decide()` above already tolerates the same input (`body?.attributes?.length` then `for...of`, yielding a 403 deny). Reachable only by a caller that passes `YorkieSignatureGuard`, which bounds the impact, but the log line is strictly less robust than the decision it reports.

samples.summary: New module comment asserts the auth webhook "allows everything" until `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true`, contradicting the enforce-by-default this same change introduces
samples.evidence: Lines 58-67 state "the webhook allows everything until a deployment both registers its methods and sets `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true`". `isYorkieAuthEnforced` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts:29) returns true for an unset variable, and the controller's own doc block (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:120) says enforcing is the default. A future reader weighing whether this wrapper's gates are still load-bearing is told the opposite of the deployment reality by a file added in the same commit. (The equivalent stale claims in `packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:40`, `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4413` and `packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:445-447` were left unupdated too.)

samples.summary: Divider drag math divides by a `track` that can be zero or negative, producing NaN/Infinity flex bases
samples.evidence: `const track = rect.width - divider.offsetWidth;` (line 544) then `const ratio = (ev.clientX - rect.left) / track;` (line 546). With a container narrower than the divider's new 25px, `track` is ≤ 0: a zero track with the pointer exactly on `rect.left` yields `0/0 = NaN`, and `Math.max(0.15, Math.min(0.85, NaN))` is NaN, so `flex: 1 1 NaN%` is written and ignored by the browser. Also, the pointer now maps to the divider's *left* edge rather than its centre, so at 25px the hairline sits ~12px right of the finger — the comment claims the trailing was eliminated.

samples.summary: PDF comment store has no read-only refusal equivalent to the new `assertWritable` in the spreadsheet store, so its CRDT writes rest on UI gating alone
samples.evidence: The change added `assertWritable` to `YorkieStore.addThread/addReply/editComment/deleteComment/setThreadResolved` (yorkie-store.ts:1310-1387) on the stated reasoning that "a UI gate is the wrong last line". `PdfCommentStore` (addThread:112, addReply:146, editComment:164, deleteComment:176, setThreadResolved:189) and `usePdfComments` (pdf-comments-controller.ts:40/56/75) carry no `readOnly` parameter at all, so the only thing between a viewer-role mount and a `doc.update()` on the CRDT root is `ThreadDetailPanel`'s `readOnly` prop (pdf-collab.tsx:377) and the `!readOnly` render gates — the exact arrangement judged insufficient for sheets. I could not find a reachable viewer-side caller today, hence low confidence, but the defence-in-depth the same commit added elsewhere is absent here.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. `ensureSlidesRoot` returns immediately on `options.readOnly` (yorkie-slides-store.ts:234), skipping the backfill `doc.update` that performs the `meta.themeId`/`meta.masterId` ↔ `themes`/`masters` reconciliation (lines 283-295) and the `notes` / text `data.blocks` non-array normalization (lines 296-310). The doc comment (lines 222-225) claims `read()` performs "the same backfill in memory through `migrateDocument`", but migrate.ts does not: `migrateDocument` (migrate.ts:77-93) only substitutes defaults when `themes`/`masters` are absent or empty and never validates `meta.themeId` against `themes`, while `migrateMeta` passes `themeId` through verbatim (migrate.ts:32). `migrateSlide` passes `notes` through unchanged (migrate.ts:141) and `migrateElement` returns non-shape elements untouched (migrate.ts:169). Consequently a deck whose stored `meta.themeId` is absent from its stored/synthesised `themes` yields a SlidesDocument on which `getActiveTheme` throws by design (render-context.ts:88-97), reached on every paint from slide-renderer.ts:213 and editor.ts:4361. Read-only mounts reach this from slides-view.tsx:285-288 and mobile-slides-view.tsx:152-154, both of which then render from `store.read()`. I searched for a compensating guard on the read path (`themes[0]` fallbacks exist in memory.ts:186/368/504, layout-edit-store.ts:91, layout-picker.ts:70, yorkie-slides-store.ts:1078/1270, backend slides-tree.ts:72) and none of them sits between `read()` and the renderer, so `already-guarded` does not apply. Mismatched state is representable in storage: backend `writeSlidesRoot` (slides-tree.ts:97-105) persists `meta.themeId` verbatim next to a caller-supplied `themes` array, and the code's own comment at yorkie-slides-store.ts:278-282 documents the reconciliation as the defense against exactly this throw. The new test (yorkie-slides-store.test.ts:94-126) only exercises `themeId: 'default-light'`, the value that happens to equal migrateDocument's injected default, so it does not cover the gap. Real, in-lane (crash / missing guard on a reachable render path), and blocking.
